_note: Independent worked examples for time, speed, distance, fuel and endurance, from the FAA's handbooks (fetched from faa.gov on 2026-11-21), never from the code. Shape and checks as reference/atmosphere.json says.

cases.name: 210 NM at a GS of 140 kt takes 1:30
cases.source: FAA-H-8083-25C (Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, 2023), ch. 16, p. 16-11, "Time T = D/GS": "The time to fly 210 NM at a GS of 140 knots is 210 ÷ 140 or 1.5 hours ... Answer: 1:30."
cases.method: The engine's book estimate is the distance over the speed with no wind, so the handbook's ground speed is given as the speed. Exact.

cases.name: 120 kt for 1 hour 45 minutes covers 210 NM
cases.source: FAA-H-8083-25C (Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, 2023), ch. 16, p. 16-11, "Distance D = GS X T": "The distance flown in 1 hour 45 minutes at a GS of 120 knots is 120 × 1.75 or 210 NM."
cases.method: Read the other way: 210 NM at 120 kt is 105 minutes. Exact.

cases.name: 400 NM at 100 kt burning 5 gal an hour: 4 hours and 20 gal
cases.source: FAA-H-8083-25C (Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, 2023), ch. 16, p. 16-12, "Fuel Consumption": "a flight of 400 NM at 100 knots GS takes 4 hours to complete. If an aircraft consumes 5 gallons of fuel per hour, the total fuel consumption is 20 gallons ... there is no wind; therefore, true airspeed (TAS) is also 100 knots".
cases.method: Exact. The handbook gives the trip's fuel only; the engine's required fuel adds a reserve, not checked here.

cases.name: 220 NM at a GS of 88 kt burning 8 gal an hour: 2:30 and about 20 gal
cases.source: FAA-H-8083-25C (Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, 2023), ch. 16, p. 16-15: "If the distance measures 220 NM, divide by the GS of 88 knots, which gives 2.5 hours, or 2:30 ... If fuel consumption is 8 gallons an hour, 8 × 2.5 or about 20 gallons is used."
cases.method: The handbook's ground speed given as the speed. Exact.

cases.name: Chickasha to Guthrie: 53 NM at 106 kt is 30 minutes
cases.source: FAA-H-8083-25C (Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, 2023), ch. 16, p. 16-21: "the GS is 106 knots and the total time is 35 minutes (30 minutes plus 5 minutes for climb) with a fuel burn of 4.7 gallons"; Figure 16-26: total 53 NM.
cases.method: Whole minutes: within 0.5. The handbook adds 5 minutes for the climb and burns 8 gal an hour over all 35 (4.7 gal); the book estimate has no climb (the nav log's navlog_with_climbs works the climb from the airplane's own figures), so only the cruise's 30 minutes is checked.

cases.name: Chickasha to Guthrie: a 11 NM leg at 106 kt is 6 minutes
cases.source: FAA-H-8083-25C (Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, 2023), ch. 16, p. 16-20, Figure 16-26 (visual flight log): the checkpoints' legs of 11, 10, 10.5, 13 and 8.5 NM at 106 kt, estimated at 6, 6, 6, 7 and 5 minutes

cases.name: 270 NM in 3 hours is a GS of 90 kt
cases.source: FAA-H-8083-25C (Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, 2023), ch. 16, p. 16-11, "GS = D/T": "If an aircraft flies 270 NM in 3 hours, the GS is 270 ÷ 3 = 90 knots."

cases.name: 38 gal usable at 8 gal an hour is 4 hours 45 minutes of fuel
cases.source: FAA-H-8083-25C (Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, 2023), ch. 16, pp. 16-19 to 16-21, Figures 16-25 to 16-27: usable fuel 38 gallons, fuel rate 8 GPH; the flight plan's item 12, fuel on board, "4 45", "determined by dividing the total usable fuel aboard in gallons by the estimated rate of fuel consumption".

cases.name: A 45-minute reserve at 16 gal an hour is 12 gal
cases.source: FAA-H-8083-1B (Aircraft Weight and Balance Handbook, 2016), ch. 6, p. 6-3: "Cruise fuel flow = 16 gallons per hour ... Reserve fuel = 45 minutes = 12 gallons".
cases.method: Exact. The handbook names no flight rules; 45 minutes is the IFR reserve (14 CFR 91.167(a)(3)) and the VFR one at night (91.151(a)(2)) alike.
